digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate — impact model calibration and verifier grading
propositions: The divergent_implementation axis fires on only 7.72% of plan-v3 findings and was never calibrated; 90% of the 1,307 omitted-scope findings are graded none despite representing real plan divergences, causing systematic under-blocking.

The axis must be retyped from ordinal (none/low/medium/high) to a closed Literal with three semantic grades (contradicts_reality, omits_required_site, incomplete_enumeration) that distinguish load-bearing divergences from cosmetic ones, with floor applications only for the first two.

The impact_plan function currently resolves all axes through _SEV01 keyed on ordinals; a schema-only change would score all three new symbolic grades as 0.0, silently disabling the axis instead of implementing the floor—requiring explicit structural refactoring to exclude divergent_implementation from _SEV01 and route it through DIVERGENCE_GRADE01 instead.

A production-impact floor (Fix 2) is rejected because it is orthogonal to plan novelty and cannot be author-remediated, making findings non-terminating under the remediation loop; Fix 1 (semantic grading) subsumes most of Fix 2's value while preserving convergence.

ADR-0054 mandates that calibration must use only data produced during normal gate use (corpus replay) or dogfooding in-field; purpose-built LLM eval suites and bulk re-review runs are rejected on cost grounds.

The verifier prompts and all prompt-side consumers (including plan_review_G7.md) must be updated to define and map the three new grades with worked examples, and the shared preamble must name both kind-graded axes to prevent the LLM from emitting now-invalid ordinal values.
